source_document.body:
Chinese PV and solar equipment brand LEAPTING has taken the wraps off its new, battery-powered Auto-Navigation Forklift Robot (AFR) designed to speed up the installation of large, utility-scale solar power projects .
The newest member in a growing lineup of fully autonomous solar construction and maintenance robots , the latest LEAPTING AFR was revealed earlier this week at a solar technology conference in Dubai, where the heavy-duty, fully autonomous and battery-powered tracked forklift was called the “missing link” in solar material handling for its ability to delivers solar module pallets directly from terminals or laydown yards to installation rows without the need to put either a human operator or flagman in harm’s way.
“The AFR combines GPS-RTK, laser-based simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), and 3D computer vision to locate pallets, identify fork-hole coordinates in real time, and auto-plan insertion paths,” the company said, in a statement. “ It further features 360-degree multi-line LiDAR , intelligent obstacle avoidance, and a three-tier braking system.”
The thing, itself
Image by LEAPTING.
The AFR uses a 48 V, 400 Ah lithium battery with a nominal capacity of 19.2 kWh, sending power to a pair of electric drive motors mounted high in the track. The combination is reportedly good for about 10 total hp and a full eight hours of continuous operation under “standard” operating conditions – more than enough, in other words, to handle a full day’s work.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
And, thanks to its IP67 all-weather protection and fully tracked, tank-like mobility, the all-terrain LEAPTING forklift robot can handle 3,000 kg (~6,600 lbs.) of solar and PV materials per load across some of the most demanding job sites you can think, from desert sand and gravel to uneven, muddy, and icy ground, giving the company a product that could, conceivably, be deployed just about anywhere tomorrow.
The company claims the new AFR can automatically mount modules on trackers every 40 seconds (3–5x faster than manual labour) with placement accuracy under +/-1mm. You can check it out for yourself in the images, above, then let us know what you think of this newest solar construction robot in the comments.

source_document.body:
Borderlands Mexico is a weekly rundown of developments in the world of United States-Mexico cross-border trucking and trade. This week in Borderlands Mexico: US trucking crackdown raises concerns over freight disruptions; M2 Global Logistics launches in Houston; and Cutter & Buck opens new distribution center in Texas.
US trucking crackdown raises concerns over freight disruptions
Stricter enforcement of U.S. trucking regulations is raising concerns about potential disruptions to cross-border freight, as American and Mexican transportation leaders warn that efforts to crack down on illegal operations must not create new obstacles for legitimate carriers .
The concerns emerged during two panel discussions at the International Road Transport Union’s (IRU) North American Transportation Forum, held during the 2026 National Convention of Mexico’s National Chamber of Freight Transportation (CANACAR) in Cancún.
Representatives from the American Trucking Associations (ATA), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Werner Enterprises and CANACAR discussed increased scrutiny of cabotage violations, B-1 visas , English-language proficiency requirements and commercial driver qualifications.
While participants generally supported stronger enforcement, several cautioned that inconsistent application of the rules could create delays, restrict driver availability and complicate freight movement between the United States and Mexico .
U.S. trucking executives back tougher enforcement
Derek Leathers, chairman and CEO of Werner Enterprises, said stronger enforcement is necessary to prevent foreign drivers from illegally transporting domestic freight within the U.S.
Under federal cabotage restrictions , foreign drivers may transport qualifying international shipments into and out of the United States but generally cannot haul domestic freight between two U.S. locations.
Leathers supported federal efforts to address the misuse of B-1 business visitor visas by drivers performing unauthorized domestic trucking operations.
He also welcomed increased enforcement by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) of English-language proficiency requirements , emphasizing the importance of drivers being able to communicate with law enforcement and other personnel while operating in the U.S.
The Trump administration has intensified enforcement of English-language proficiency standards for commercial drivers, alongside efforts to tighten oversight of driver licensing and training.
Leathers’ comments reflect growing support among U.S. trucking executives for stricter enforcement against carriers and drivers operating outside federal requirements.
However, the discussions also highlighted concerns that increased scrutiny could affect compliant Mexican carriers engaged in legitimate international freight transportation.
ATA economist calls for fair enforcement
ATA Chief Economist Bob Costello emphasized the need for consistent and proportionate enforcement, particularly as cross-border freight activity continues to recover.
Costello said North American cross-border trade rebounded in 2026 following a slight decline in 2025, underscoring the importance of maintaining efficient transportation links between the U.S., Mexico and Canada.
According to Mexican transportation publication Revista Transportes y Turismo , Costello also raised concerns that some U.S. enforcement personnel may not fully understand the complexities of cabotage regulations.
The potential for inconsistent interpretations could create uncertainty for Mexican carriers operating legally in the U.S.
Costello called for continued cooperation among transportation associations, regulators and industry representatives to ensure that enforcement efforts target violations without unnecessarily disrupting legitimate freight movements.
Mexican carriers warn of border delays
CANACAR President Augusto Ramos Melo acknowledged the importance of combating illegal cabotage but warned that intensified border enforcement could create additional delays and operational challenges for Mexican trucking companies.
Ramos called for closer coordination among transportation companies, customs officials and other supply chain participants to improve border efficiency.
His concerns come as Mexican carriers navigate tighter scrutiny of driver documentation, visa eligibility and compliance with U.S. transportation regulations.
For carriers operating across the southern border, additional inspections and documentation requirements can complicate driver scheduling, equipment positioning and delivery times.
Martin Rojas, IRU’s senior adviser for the Americas, moderated the discussions and emphasized the importance of balancing regulatory enforcement with the need to maintain an adequate supply of qualified drivers.
The discussions highlighted the challenge facing policymakers: strengthening compliance without undermining the transportation capacity needed to support North American trade.
CBP outlines new border initiatives
Liliana Flores, CBP’s port director at Del Rio, Texas, said the agency is working to improve how it processes trade information while expanding initiatives aimed at strengthening cargo security, according to Revista Transportes y Turismo .
Flores discussed developments involving the Customs Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (CTPAT), a voluntary public-private partnership designed to strengthen international supply chain security.
Flores encouraged Mexican trucking companies to participate in CTPAT and CBP’s Electronic Export Manifest pilot program.
The pilot’s testing period is scheduled to conclude Oct. 23, with information collected during the program intended to help CBP refine its systems ahead of broader implementation.
The initiatives are intended to improve security and the exchange of shipment information, although carriers continue to face increased scrutiny of cross-border operations.
Visa requirements and driver shortages
The second panel examined how regulatory changes are affecting drivers and transportation companies.
Justen Thomas, a representative of the U.S. Consulate General, advised drivers applying for or renewing B-1 visas to prepare thoroughly for consular interviews.
Thomas said English-language proficiency is among several factors that can influence visa decisions.
B-1 visas are commonly used by eligible Mexican commercial drivers transporting international freight into the United States. However, those visas do not authorize drivers to perform domestic cabotage operations.
IRU Goods Transport Council President Iro Doumani offered a European perspective, describing how coordinated regulatory systems and digitalization can help balance enforcement with efficient international freight transportation.
Doumani also noted that driver shortages remain a challenge for transportation operators, even in regions with more integrated cross-border systems.
The panelists agreed that closer cooperation among regulators, customs agencies and trucking companies would be necessary to maintain efficient freight movement while strengthening compliance.
M2 Global Logistics launches in Houston with 830,000-square-foot facility
Meiborg Companies and Morales Capital Group have partnered to launch M2 Global Logistics, a new third-party logistics provider anchored by an 830,000-square-foot industrial campus near downtown Houston.
The companies announced the venture Thursday, saying the new logistics platform will combine Meiborg’s trucking and warehousing operations with Morales Capital Group’s international trade and investment capabilities.
The 27-acre Houston campus will provide access to major freight corridors, intermodal hubs and port connections. The facility is expected to begin operations in the coming months, with additional market expansion planned.
“This partnership evolves a proven regional operation into a truly global 3PL brand,” said Zach Meiborg, CEO of Meiborg Companies, in a statement.
Founded in 1981 and headquartered in Rockford, Illinois, Meiborg operates more than 550 trucks and manages over 4 million square feet of warehouse space across Illinois and Texas.
M2 Global Logistics plans to offer domestic trucking, international freight services, customs-related logistics, warehousing, fulfillment and distribution under one platform.
The new company will be led by Zach Meiborg, Nick Gibbons and James Cooper, alongside executives from Morales Capital Group.
Cutter & Buck opens new distribution center in Texas
Apparel company Cutter & Buck has opened a new distribution center in Grand Prairie, Texas, expanding its fulfillment network to better serve customers across the central and southern U.S.
The facility, which opened Oct. 7, is the company’s fourth distribution center in North America and will stock sportswear from Cutter & Buck, Clique and Craft, according to a company announcement .
Located in the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, the distribution center will provide additional inventory capacity and support faster order fulfillment for customers nationwide.
The facility offers weekday UPS and FedEx pickups, along with local customer pickup services and the company’s Share Ship order fulfillment program.
Cutter & Buck also plans to introduce in-house embroidery and heat-transfer services at the facility during the first quarter of 2027. The company said the operation is currently undergoing testing, with capacity expected to increase over the coming months.
Why it matters: Stricter trucking enforcement could complicate driver availability and border operations, adding uncertainty for carriers and shippers moving freight between the United States and Mexico.

This Toyota Sienna Was Transformed Into a Stealthy, Off-Road Ready Micro Camper Van
14 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Horizon Camper Builds
There are various reasons why someone would want to stealth camp, from more security to total privacy, and more. The best stealth camping in a van is done in smaller rigs, as they're, in my opinion, way more inconspicuous compared to larger models. Today, I'd like to discuss a cleverly built stealth camper packing a bunch of comforts.
What we have here is a conversion based on a 2026 AWD Toyota Sienna with a Woodland edition. It was done by Horizon Camper Builds, a Watsonville, California-based company specializing in converting standard minivans and medium to full-size SUVs into versatile, custom camper mobiles.
The company hand-builds kits from solid wood, designed to offer unmatched rigidity, longevity, and a perfectly secure fit. It has three build levels, from an entry-level package to a package that transforms the vehicle into a fully self-sustained off-grid camper.
This rig has the Level 2 package, which builds upon the solid foundation of the Level 1 by adding smart storage solutions. All of the company's kits are removable, so you can return the van to a passenger vehicle configuration.
This rig's customer wants to do either stealth camping or outdoor camping while making use of the van's AWD capabilities. You can tell that they're fully enjoying the AWD capabilities by the exterior mods they made, instantly noticeable as soon as you lay eyes on the van.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Horizon Camper Builds The vehicle rides on black alloy wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires, which pair nicely with the grey paint job. The customer fitted a 2-inch (5-centimeter) lift kit, which created additional ground clearance and made room for the larger tires. What's more, at the front, you'll come across a beefy front guard for the bumper.
That's it for the exterior - that's why I said that it's stealthy. It could easily pass as a Sienna modified into an off-roader – there are no upgrades that hint toward the "camper DNA." What's more, the windows are tinted, so you can't see anything going on inside.
The van comes with two powered sliding doors, but only the one on the passenger side is an entrance, as the other is slightly blocked by furniture.
The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. However, you can use a curtain to divide the two areas for more privacy. Even though all the windows are tinted, WeatherTech window covers allow you to fully darken the interior when needed.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Horizon Camper Builds Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for carbon grey-stained cabinetry that matches the exterior paint and a black carpeted floor.
The driver's side of the living space is taken up by a single-sized bed with an inflatable mattress provided by the customer that measures 70 inches (178 centimeters) in length and 28 inches (71 centimeters) in width. Usually, the company provides tri-fold mattresses for its builds.
There is space for an adult to sleep here, but I wouldn't say that it would be too comfortable. Luckily, you can create a double bed sleeping platform that's 75 inches (190 centimeters) long and 50 inches (127 centimeters) wide.
The bed can double as a couch, with a shelving system behind the bed doubling as a backrest. This system integrates two cubbies.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Horizon Camper Builds On the opposite side, you'll come across a storage unit with a top and a flip-up table. This is where you can enjoy a meal or do some work on your laptop. The countertop extends toward the back of the build, providing more surface area you can take advantage of. Moreover, on the side of the counter, you'll find two standard outlets and a USB plug, with matching charging points on the cubby unit.
Speaking about power, you'll find the van's "electrical heart" underneath the rear part of the countertop. It's a Bluetti AC200 portable power station with a 1,700 Wh of battery capacity and a maximum AC output of 2,000 W.
Next to it, there's a small drawer that can only be accessed from the outside, after opening the trunk door. Furthermore, below the countertop, Horizon Camper Builds added an Iceco chest-style fridge/freezer.
Basically, you can keep the trunk door open and use the countertop and the features I mentioned as part of an outdoor kitchen. You also get a large water container with an electric dispenser.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Horizon Camper Builds There's a bit of space left between the driver and passenger seats so that you get the full adjustability front and back for the two seats. This setup also leaves room for you to access two cup holders and an AC outlet that came with the van. By the way, the vehicle came with a built-in 1,500 W inverter.
All in all, this camper van by Horizon Camper Builds might be small but it packs all the essentials and offers abundant storage space. Sure, you won't be able to live in it full-time, but it's perfect for a weekend adventure, especially if you want to blend in in urban environments and not have people think twice of your van.

2026 Paris Motor Show • Hyundai Tucson N Line Steals the Spotlight in Paris, but It's All Show and No Go
Alfa Romeo’s Cuorerosso Concept Gives Birth to the New Giulia Sportwagon in Fantasy Land
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik
The 2026 Paris Motor Show is officially closing its gates today, October 18, 2026, after it opened them at the beginning of the week, and the event has witnessed quite a few premieres from several brands.
Sure, it hasn’t been that exciting as it used to be a few years ago, but then again, this applies to all major international auto shows. That’s because most automakers are not interested in blowing a huge amount of money just to have several rides on display for a few days, as they could get a lot more reach by taking to the World Wide Web, and for far less money. Thus, the automotive shows as we know them are slowly but steadily dying.
Mind you, we haven’t gathered here to talk about auto shows as a whole, not the big premieres unveiled in France’s capital city, but to put the spotlight on a single one: the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso . Surely I cannot be the only one who thinks that this thing looks very good, right? Actually, that would be a no, because the study has been praised by petrolheads of all ages ever since it broke cover in Paris at the beginning of the week.
So much so that it has also ended up in the hands of rendering artists, or a small chunk of the pixel-altering crowd to be more precise, becoming something else, while retaining its cool DNA. One of our latest encounters with such a thing came from @kelsonik on Instagram, who dropped the digital illustrations shared in our image gallery a few days ago. These imagine the cool-looking concept as a station wagon, and the CGI manipulator refers to the project as the Alfa Romeo Giulia Sportwagon.
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik You see, the Italian car marque hasn’t had such a thing in its lineup ever since the 159 . You do remember the sports sedan built between 2004 and 2011, don’t you? Why, of course you do, as its design is hard to forget, and that’s a good thing, because it looked very cool back then, and it still looks cool to this day. But the 159 wasn’t strictly offered as a four-door sedan, as a five-door estate joined it, and it added the Sportwagon suffix.
Both featured a front-engine and either front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive. They were based on the GM/Fiat Premium platform, just like the Brera, Spider, and Visconti Concept. The powertrain family comprises a few straight-four units, a V6, and three diesels, which were mated, depending on the configuration, to a five-speed manual, a six-speed manual, or a six-speed auto ‘box. The 159 preceded the 156, and it was succeeded by the Giulia from 2015.
The latter is thus an aging product, as it will turn 12 next year, yet that does not mean that it is not on the cool side of the premium compact segment, because it is, especially in the Quadrifoglio specification, not to mention the even more exotic GTA and GTAm. The old FCA Giorgio platform sits beneath the skin, and it is shared with its crossover sibling, the Stelvio.
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik Now, given that Alfa Romeo no longer has a station wagon in its lineup, and that the Giulia continues to live on as a four-door sedan, it is obvious why the rendering artist quoted above has decided to unofficially christen this CGI model the Giulia Sportwagon. It features the same front fascia as the Cuorerosso Concept, has a much longer roofline, traditional rear doors, flush handles, different rear three-quarter panels, and redesigned rear three-quarter windows.
The changes continue out back, where this machine features different rear pillars, a tailgate that opens up into a generous cargo area, and a spoiler. Everything else soldiers on from the show car, including the taillights, rear bumper, diffuser, Alfa Romeo emblem, and so on. The car is finished in the same red color, and rides on the same gold wheels.
As you already know, the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso is a 2+2 four-door model, and it packs the same engine as the Giulia Quadrifoglio and the Stelvio Quadrifoglio. The company hasn’t detailed the powertrain, but we know that the 2.9-liter twin-turbo V6, which boasts Ferrari DNA, develops 505 hp and 442 lb-ft (600 Nm) of torque, and 533 horsepower in the GTA and GTAm versions of the Giulia.
It is likely that the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso won’t hit the assembly line, but some of the design cues could be found on future models from the Italian car marque. And to be honest, we want to see this thing in production, with only a few tweaks, as it would be a proper rival to the likes of the BMW M3 , Audi RS 5 Sedan, and Mercedes- AMG C 63. Not to mention that the Sportwagon flavor would allow it to tackle the five-door versions of these cars. View this post on Instagram A post shared by CAR DESIGN | RENDERINGS (@kelsonik)

This 1959 Chevy Bel Air Might Look Abandoned, but What a Big Surprise It Hides Under the Hood
18 photos
Photo: Street Dreams Texas
Say what you want about this Bel Air, but once you open the hood, you’ll change your mind. The car is a project that needs a complete restoration, and despite no longer having the original engine under the hood, it does have enough power to convince you to save it.
The car was purchased by Street Dreams Texas as part of a Bel Air trio, and the reason why it’s here is as simple as it could be: it must convince an Internet stranger to take it home and begin the restoration process it’s been dreaming about for what could be decades.
This isn’t an easy project, but a 1959 Bel Air could be worth the effort. This was the year when the Impala and the Bel Air became separate series. The Impala was now the top full-size Chevrolet, while the Bel Air was considered the more affordable version, despite sharing most parts, engines, and styling with its sibling.
For example, the 1959 Bel Air was available with the same engine options as the Impala, including the top 348 big-block unit. The 348 debuted in 1958 and was the best you could go for in the full-size Chevrolet world both in its first and its second year on the market.
This Bel Air no longer has the original engine under the hood. It’s now fitted with a 454ci big-block engine from another Chevrolet produced at some point between the ‘70s and the early ‘90s. No other specifics were shared, but the dealer trying to sell the car explains that the exact engine information is unknown, so the best thing you can do is ask your mechanic to check it out in person.
At first glance, the Bel Air looks complete, though it goes without saying that you shouldn’t assume everything is in tip-top shape. The photos speak for themselves and suggest that the metal would require the typical repairs. However, as the dealer itself emphasizes, you should go there in person and see this Bel Air with your own eyes before making an offer.
The selling price makes perfect sense, though this Bel Air will have a hard time finding a buyer for two reasons. First, it’s no longer original, and second, it’s not an Impala. Once the Impala came to be, the Bel Air kind of became the backup plan for Chevrolet buyers. This is still the case for collectors, who would rather get an Impala rather than a Bel Air.
The dealer wants $7,500 for this Bel Air, though the Make Offer option is also enabled this time. This means the dealer is willing to listen to whatever you have in mind about this car. If you want to see the car live, you can find it parked in Fredericksburg, Texas.

2026 Paris Motor Show • OMODA 4 Lands in Paris To Showcase Futuristic Styling, Looks Like a Discount Urus
Lifted 1983 Chevrolet K20 Is Up For Grabs With Room For Two Up Front and Another Two In the Back!
9 photos
Photo: Garage Kept Motors / Instagram
Sitting proudly in the inventory of Grand Rapids, Michigan-based Garage Kept Motors , this high-riding 1983 Chevrolet C/K 20 Series is actively screaming “look at me, ma” from a tall place.
Before anyone thought about the Silverado and Sierra, there was the Chevrolet and GMC C/K series of trucks produced by General Motors between 1959 and 2002 in the United States and a little while longer in other places, like Mexico (2006).
Sold by both the Chevrolet and GMC divisions, the C/K series was the direct enemy of the Ford F-Series just as it was rising to stardom, and became increasingly popular over the years thanks to its encompassing and wide range of models. Used for the model branding directly from the internal model codes, the ‘C’ letter was attributed to models with two-wheel drive, while ‘K’ stood for 4WD.
Over the years, there have been four generations of Chevrolet models and three for GMC, as the latter adopted the Sierra moniker one iteration earlier, and both GM and the fans came up with nicknames, like the official Action Line and Rounded Line for the second and third generation or the Square Body plus OBS designations by enthusiasts.
As such, this big red truck which “checks all the boxes (‘¾ Ton, Red, V8, Lifted, Room for Two In The Back’) for a lifted classic Chevy and looks ready to hit the dirt” is a Square Body, a 1983 Chevrolet K20 of the classic 4x4 variety “that combines rugged styling with a selection of performance upgrades.” It’s finished in the most classic ways: crimson over a black interior and “has been built with an emphasis on V8 performance while retaining the practical character and proportions that make the square-body Chevrolet trucks so desirable.”
Under its towering hood resides a 5.7-liter V8 “equipped with angled-plug heads, an Edelbrock intake manifold, Holley carburetor, and Hedman headers,” giving a performance-focused style due to the combination of upgraded induction and exhaust components, while the engine in itself “retains the straightforward mechanical character associated with this generation of Chevrolet trucks.”
Power is routed through a 700R4 automatic transmission, including overdrive, and a 4.10 limited-slip rear end complements the setup to suit the “truck's lifted, off-road-oriented stance.” The chassis and suspension setup are highlighted by the massive lift and combine with large off-road tires and polished aluminum wheels visible from across the parking lot at any angle, for sure.
What’s very important is that the dealership isn’t asking a ton of money for this truck: it has 114 miles on the odometer, most likely since the build was finished, and it’s offered at $36,900. That’s not even enough to buy a 2026 Silverado 1500 base truck, let alone the upcoming all-new generation coming for the 2027 model year with even higher MSRPs.

source_document.body:
2026 Paris Motor Show • OMODA 4 Lands in Paris To Showcase Futuristic Styling, Looks Like a Discount Urus
26 New Premium Diecast Collectibles for October of 2026
96 photos
Photo: Tarmac Works
Sometimes I feel like we’re living in a golden era for collecting diecast models. It’s like we’ve got access to more manufacturers and collectibles than ever before. And the fierce market competition is constantly pushing the companies involved to raise the stakes in terms of both quality and quantity.
It’s all fun and games if you can either exercise restraint in spending your hard earned money, or if you don’t have to worry about draining out your account in the first place.
If you ask for an opinion outside of the hobby, it could all seem delusional as people are literally trading their money for “trinkets”. At the end of the day, that tiny Ferrari F50 won’t help pay for your bills if God forbid you ever desperately need to go that far.
Ultimately, you should use some common sense and not bite off than you can chew. Choose a type of vehicle you love and stick with it.
Don’t even think about getting them all! I’ve got 26 new premium diecast collectibles here today, and I’ll only be adding two or three of them to my must-have list.
Inno64 Photo: Inno64 Inno64’s latest release is definitely up there with my favorites. I’ve been following Mad Mike for almost 20 years now, and he’s part of the reason why I became obsessed with the Mazda RX-7 .
I’ve seen many FD builds over the years, and this is without doubt one of the most iconic variations out there. This release fits my objective to expand my 1/64th-scale drift collection, which is already looking decent enough with a few D1GP machines built by Mini GT and Tarmac Works .
Also, it’s so refreshing to see a tiny RX-7 that doesn’t have a Liberty Walk kit on it, as the old school way of doing things was so much better. It seems that production will be limited to only 3,000 pieces, and a Chase iteration could pop up if you’re lucky enough.
It’s not something I’m particularly interested in, as I’m just as happy exploring more of what this brand has to offer in the first place.
Pop Race Photo: Pop Race I’m under the impression that Pop Race ’s position in the market isn’t quite as stable compared to MiniGT and Tarmac Works. Some models look great, others feel downright boring.
Also, this Tooned car trend just doesn’t seem to work in the premium part of the hobby. I don’t mind occasionally getting one from Hot Wheels where it only costs $2 or less, but I would never pay as much as $20 for something like the Pandem Pocket Bunny 32.
Perhaps I’d feel different about it if I was still a kid and had one in front of me. The Pandem 15 features a similar color scheme, and it seems to be a replica of Echo Gao’s drift car.
She used to drift a GT86, and you can also find her pink R32 over at Inno64 if you’re a fan. There are two more APAxpo -special items you can buy, and they’re both Mercedes-AMG GT3 race cars (Uno Racing).
Photo: Pop Race I haven’t seen these before, as I by no means aim to keep a close eye on every single GT Racing series out there. There are three more cars you can pre-order for Q1 of 2027, and two of them are Lamborghini s.
The Veneno ranks higher on my list for three reasons: it has a removable engine cover (whereas the Countach LPI 800-4 has an opening front and rear hood), it looks considerably more menacing from the get-go, and Verde Ithaca is much nicer than Verde Themis from where I’m at.
There’s no new tooling for Pop Race this time, but you can join the Liberty Walk hype train with the two Hong Kong Exclusive Collection models that are both painted Gold (the RX-7 and the S15).
The manufacturer will be making 1,500 units for each of the two variations of these castings, and it’s the kind of artificial scarcity I don’t plan on subscribing to.
Mini GT Photo: MiniGT This new Mini GT pre-order went live a few days ago, and you still have until around the 26th of October to secure your chance at getting them. As always, you’ll need some patience beyond that point, as deliveries won’t start until March of 2027.
We’ve got seven items on the list instead of the usual six, as one of them has fewer wheels. That’s right, there’s a motorcycle in here, and the Ducati Panigale V4 S also features a rider. I could be wrong and he might just be someone’s who’s passing by.
Are those the kind of jeans a Ducati rider would typically wear? It would have been nicer if he at least had a helmet and some gloves on, but I’m being nitpicky here. Europe is the dominant force in this pre-order, as the Ducati is one of five items hailing from the old continent.
We haven’t seen the Liberty Walk kitted Lamborghini Countach sporting this shade of green before, and it’s not the kind of style I’m interested in. I can say the same thing about the Porsche 911 GT3 RS, which isn’t a common occurrence given how fond I am of this vehicle.
Photo: MiniGT The BMW Z3 was just recently available in red, and I may have ordered one from my dealer already. I may be getting old as I’m beginning to prefer seeing bone stock vehicles instead of highly modified ones.
I have no clue why my feed has been getting bombarded with Ben Affleck-related stories lately, although it might have something to do with his business ventures. In one of the videos that popped on my feed he was opening the door to a Mercedes-EQS for J-Lo to get in and it reminded me of the “I learn celebrity gossip against my will” meme.
Now, the same cars pop up in this new Mini GT pre-order, and it must be just a coincidence. Moving on to the Japan, the Toyota 2000GT looks stunning in that Pegasus White finish with what seems to be a wooden steering wheel inside the cabin.
You can order this as either a RHD or LHD, which isn’t something I remember seeing other manufacturers do. The Nissan GT-R is in stark contrast with the Toyota, sporting that black-on-black look for a more menacing aura. Even though I know how hard it can be to photograph vehicles in this color, I’d still want a closer look.
Tarmac Works Photo: Tarmac Works Over in the Tarmac Works camp, we aren’t dealing with a pre-order. You can head on over to the company’s website and buy them today! A new drop is coming in roughly two weeks from now, but let’s focus on what we can enjoy as we speak.
Some of the presentation photos are absolutely beautiful, and I yearn to have access to these sort of dioramas at home. I just unboxed the Pagani Utopia a few days ago and can read all about it if you’re a fan of the model.
Mine had the carbon fiber finish and accurate wheels (which I complained about), whereas this blue variation uses the same rims left and right! It only costs $11.90 before taxes, as it’s part of the Global64 line-up.
The Pagani Zonda R is a bit more impressive by comparison, which is why it costs $21.90. I want one yesterday as it’s one of my Top 10 all-time favorites.
Photo: Tarmac Works It makes the Aston Martin DBS Superleggera look tame by comparison, but I’m sure some people might prefer the latter over the track-only Italian machine.
I would skip both the Honda Ballade Sports MUGEN CR-X PRO (second-gen is better), and the VERTEX Toyota Soarer JZZ30 (nothing beats the D1GP version) just to have the VERTEX Toyota Aristo JZS161.
The only problem is the latter is a TOC MOM (Tarmac Owner Club Members Only Model) edition. I’ve wanted to sign up for some time now! I quite like the choice of wheels on the Furusato RWB 993 compared to the Army Girl, but as mentioned before I think I’d rather stick to the factory look on this one too. The LB-Super Silhouette Nissan SILVIA (S15) Drift is part of the Hobby64 collection, and it only costs half as much as the 1/43rd scale variation.
The latter provides a closer look at the turbocharged 4-rotor setup under the bonnet, which is enough to justify the price difference in my eyes. The Pandem Toyota GR Yaris should have had the same feature. I saved one 1/64th-scale collectible as a surprise in the photo gallery, and it has something to do with Monsters Inc! Which one of these cars will you be going after?
